course_title: AI Computing Continuum: Extending AI Beyond the Hyperscale Data Center
course_subtitle: Open infrastructure for distributed, specialized, and increasingly disaggregated AI inference

term_glossary.tooltip: OCP project for open, modular AI infrastructure across hyperscale-adjacent environments.
Diverse compute environments outside centralized hyperscale data centers that can reuse hyperscale innovations.
Point of Presence: a service-provider site where networks or compute services connect to users and other networks.
Network and interconnect infrastructure carrying traffic for AI workloads and services.
Stored key-value state reused while an inference service generates later output tokens.
The inference phase that processes the input context and creates the initial model state.
The iterative inference phase that generates output tokens using accumulated model state.
A model for expanding or moving compute capacity across geographic regions.
IOWN-proposed model for keeping data or system state synchronized across sites.
IOWN-proposed model for real-time access between a local environment and remote AI services or resources.
Control of data according to applicable location, governance, and lifecycle requirements.
Evidence used to assess the identity and state of a computing environment before trusting it with a workload.
Joint technical and economic evaluation of whether a design can be deployed sustainably.

cards.title: Batch
cards.body: Throughput, cost, and energy can matter more than immediate response.

cards.title: Interactive
cards.body: Time to first token, token latency, and tail behavior shape the experience.

cards.title: Agentic
cards.body: Long, growing context and tool calls create stateful, bursty demand.

cards.title: Multimodal
cards.body: Text, images, audio, and sensor inputs place different demands on the system.

cards.title: Physical AI
cards.body: Predictable response and safe local operation can be essential.

cards.title: Small Local Models
cards.body: Quantized models can trade broad capacity for local latency, privacy, and efficiency.

slides.title: Connectivity Alone Is Not Enough

bullets.text: A region may not be able to grow another large facility.
An enterprise may need data to remain in an approved location.
Some applications need compute near the point of use.
A smaller site may need temporary access to specialized resources.

figure.alt: Available compute capacity increases from limited to expanded while connectivity increases from isolated to connected.
figure.caption: Capacity increases horizontally, connectivity improves vertically, and useful remote compute requires both.

slides.title: The Case for AICC in Four Ideas
items: Inference demand begins in many environments.
Hyperscale adjacent is a spectrum, not one edge tier.
Connectivity joins scale as a core placement decision.

slides.title: Check Your Understanding: Why AICC
slides.subtitle: Answer both questions once to continue. Correctness is not required, and you can retry.

questions.prompt: What is the primary infrastructure change motivating AICC?

choices.text: Inference is spreading across environments with different physical and operational requirements.
All AI processing is consolidating into one standard hyperscale facility design.
choices.feedback_incorrect: AICC responds to increasing distribution and diversity, not consolidation into one facility design.

choices.text: Networking is replacing the need for compute infrastructure.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Connectivity complements compute capacity; it does not replace the compute, memory, storage, or facility layers.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. Inference is expanding across diverse sites and workload profiles.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Review why inference changes where compute must operate.

questions.prompt: Which statements belong to the AICC problem space?

choices.text: Telecom points of presence, enterprise facilities, factories, and offices can be hyperscale adjacent.
Latency, sovereignty, power, cooling, and availability can influence placement.
Every inference request should be sent to the largest available data center.
Every site can use identical infrastructure and operating assumptions.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. AICC spans diverse environments and placement constraints.
questions.feedback_incorrect: AICC does not assume one site design or one universal placement decision.

slides.title: Five Domains Turn the Vision into Hardware Work

cards.title: AI Open Server Architectures
cards.body: Server and sled form factors, heterogeneous accelerators, fabrics, and mechanical, electrical, and thermal interfaces.

cards.title: AI Open Solution Architectures
cards.body: Rack and system designs, cooling, power delivery, facility constraints, retrofit, and modular deployment.

cards.title: AI Building Block Architectures
cards.body: Reusable enclosures, cooling modules, networking modules, and power distribution or conversion.

cards.title: Autonomous AI Wireless Access
cards.body: Open radio components and interfaces for autonomous AI-enabled wireless environments.

cards.title: Connectivity
cards.body: AI fabrics and Scale-Across communications within and between deployments.

slides.title: Common Building Blocks Must Fit Very Different Sites

bullets.text: Power, cooling, floor loading, footprint, and retrofit constraints.
Temperature, dust, vibration, acoustics, and enclosure protection.
Remote management, technician skills, service access, and recovery.
Add racks, add modules, or replace within a fixed physical envelope.

figure.alt: Four hyperscale-adjacent site profiles with different power, cooling, environment, and service constraints.
figure.caption: Open interfaces enable adaptation; they do not require identical deployments.

slides.title: A Modular Toolkit for Diverse Deployments
items: Five connected domains divide the current hardware work.
Standard boundaries can support different site implementations.
Within one serving deployment, inference can separate compute, memory, cache, storage, fabrics, telemetry, and trust across specialized resources.
The goal is meaningful interoperability and software choice, not one universal platform.

slides.subtitle: Answer both questions once to continue. Correctness is not required, and you can retry.

questions.prompt: Which AICC domain most directly addresses rack-level cooling, power delivery, and deployment constraints?

choices.text: AI Open Solution Architectures
Autonomous AI Wireless Access
choices.feedback_incorrect: Wireless Access addresses radio components and interfaces rather than rack-level cooling and power.

choices.text: Connectivity
choices.feedback_incorrect: Connectivity addresses AI fabrics and communications rather than the complete rack and facility solution.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. AI Open Solution Architectures covers rack, cooling, power, facility, and deployment considerations.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Review the distinction between server, solution, building-block, wireless, and connectivity work.

questions.prompt: Which considerations can change across hyperscale-adjacent sites?

choices.text: Cooling method and available power
Environmental exposure and service model
Physical footprint and growth model
The requirement that every site use an identical rack

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. Open interfaces must support adaptation across those constraints.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Openness standardizes useful boundaries; it does not require identical site implementations.

slides.title: Across Patterns You Will Distinguish
slides.subtitle: By the end of this module, you will be able to:
objectives: Recognize capacity, synchronization, and reach scenarios.
Explain the primary behavior of each Across model.
Identify bandwidth, latency, availability, security, and sovereignty requirements.
Connect a design to measurable workload service objectives.

reference_links.label: IOWN perspective: the three Across models

slides.title: Scale-Across Distributes Capacity Across Regions

bullets.text: Expand, divide, or move useful compute capacity across geographic regions.
Power, cooling, space, utilization, demand, and regional availability.
Resource discovery, topology, data placement, secure access, and telemetry.
Distribution must preserve performance, governance, reliability, energy, and cost objectives.

figure.alt: Workloads and capacity distributed across three geographic regions with different power and availability conditions.
figure.caption: Available devices are useful only when the complete workload can meet its objective.

reference_links.label: NVIDIA: origin of the Scale-Across term

slides.title: Sync-Across Keeps Data and State Consistent

figure.alt: Animated transaction showing local processing, a remote write-ahead-log commit, acknowledgment, primary-site interruption, and recovery from synchronized state.
figure.caption: The network round trip becomes part of application response time when acknowledgment depends on remote durability.

slides.title: Reach-Across Brings Remote AI Resources to the User

bullets.text: Give a local user, device, or application real-time access to a remote AI resource.
Research parks, enterprises, industrial sites, mobile services, and carrier-neutral edge.
Discovery, attestation, connectivity, sovereignty, availability, and cost control.
Find-connect-compute and zero-trust sharing remain target capabilities.

figure.alt: A research park accessing remote accelerator capacity while protected data remains governed locally.
figure.caption: Reach-Across is real-time service access, not simply preloading data into a remote cloud.

slides.title: Choose the Across Model by Workload Need
items: Reach-Across addresses real-time access to remote resources.
Service objectives determine whether distribution is useful.
A complete design may combine all three patterns.

slides.title: Check Your Understanding: Across Models
slides.subtitle: Answer both questions once to continue. Correctness is not required, and you can retry.

questions.prompt: A research park needs short-term access to a remote accelerator while retaining local governance of sensitive data. Which model best describes the primary need?

choices.text: Reach-Across
Sync-Across
choices.feedback_incorrect: Sync-Across focuses on keeping state consistent; the primary need here is real-time access to a remote resource.

choices.text: Scale-Up
choices.feedback_incorrect: Scale-Up increases capacity inside a tightly connected system rather than reaching a remote service.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. Reach-Across centers on real-time access to a remote capability.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Classify the scenario by its primary purpose.

questions.prompt: Which statements correctly describe the Across models?

choices.text: Scale-Across can address capacity constrained by regional power or space.
Sync-Across asks what state must remain consistent and how quickly.
Reach-Across depends on discovery, trust, connectivity, and service objectives.
Each model requires one prescribed network technology.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. The models describe workload purposes and requirements, not one mandatory technology.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Separate the workload purpose from the implementation technology.

slides.thank_you_message: Nice work—you've finished Module 3: Three Ways to Compute Across Distance.

slides.title: AICC Is an Open, Evolving Hardware Ecosystem
items: AICC addresses distributed inference across diverse environments.
The current scope covers five connected hardware domains.

OCP and IOWN bring complementary ecosystem strengths.
Current contributions can shape the project's boundaries and priorities.

slides.title: Check Your Understanding: Ecosystem Action
slides.subtitle: Answer both questions once to continue. Correctness is not required, and you can retry.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the complementary roles of OCP and the IOWN Global Forum?

choices.text: OCP develops open hardware ecosystem contributions, while IOWN brings communications architecture, use cases, validation, and techno-economic analysis.
Both organizations independently define the same complete software platform.
choices.feedback_incorrect: The collaboration joins complementary hardware, communications, use-case, and validation strengths rather than duplicating one software platform.

choices.text: IOWN certifies OCP hardware products without using industry use cases.
choices.feedback_incorrect: IOWN's role emphasizes communications architecture, vertical use cases, reference designs, proof of concept, and economic analysis.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. The partnership connects specifications and supplier engagement to use cases, communications architecture, and validation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Review how the two ecosystems meet between user needs and implementation.

questions.prompt: Which are responsible ways to describe or advance AICC?

choices.text: Treat find-connect-compute and zero-trust sharing as target capabilities.
Coordinate with adjacent OCP work rather than recreate it.
Bring use cases, requirements, designs, and validation data to the community.
Describe AICC as a completed common product already deployed across vendors.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. AICC is an evolving project whose target capabilities require community specification and validation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Keep current project work distinct from proposed models and completed products.
